params.prompt:
1950s theatrical cartoon slapstick, hand-drawn colored-pencil pencil-test animation on cream paper, held on twos with visible line boil. Fixed camera, locked tripod, one continuous shot.

The young man in the office chair, facing us and smiling, lifts his right hand off the armrest and points sharply up and away over his right shoulder towards the far left of the frame, holds the point, and gives one small approving nod. He swings the point down and to the left, low and close towards the camera, and nods once. He swings it straight out at the camera, past us, and nods once. He swings it up and away over his left shoulder towards the far right of the frame, and nods once. Then he opens both hands palms up in a small "go on" gesture, drops them back onto the armrests, and settles, smiling, with one last slow nod.

His mouth stays one small closed smile in every frame. His eyes stay open in every frame, following each point. His short blonde hair, his stubble and his navy T-shirt are the same in every frame. He stays seated in the same chair on the same spot on the floor in every frame, and the chair stays turned towards us in every frame. The desk, the three monitors, the cork board, the whiteboard, the printer bench, the shelf of binders, the lamp, the mug, the bell and the striped cannon stay the same drawings in every frame.

Squash and stretch on every accent, smear frames through the fast arcs, snappy timing, elastic overshoot, comic energy.
